## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater green alga belonging to the desmids, characterized by large, strongly curved crescent-shaped cells with broad, slightly recurved tips. Closterium submoniliferum closely resembles Closterium moniliferum but is generally larger and has numerous small pyrenoids scattered throughout its chloroplasts rather than arranged in a single central row. Its cell wall appears smooth at low magnification but is finely striated when examined more closely. It occurs in freshwater ponds, wetlands, and other standing waters, particularly in moderately nutrient-rich waters with near-neutral pH. Like other desmids, it contributes to aquatic primary production and the microscopic food web.
